title: GenomicsContentFormats
description: Enumerates supported genomics content formats. Uses oneOf with const+description so each value is self-documented.

oneOf.description: Binary Alignment/Map: binary, indexed representation of aligned sequencing reads (SAM in BGZF).
Browser Extensible Data: genomic intervals/annotations; commonly for features and tracks.
CRAM: reference-based compressed alternative to BAM to reduce storage size.
FASTA: plaintext sequences (nucleotide or amino acid); may include multiple records.
FASTQ: sequences with per-base quality scores; standard for raw reads.
MPEG-G: ISO/IEC family for efficient genomic data representation and transport.
Sequence Alignment/Map: text-based alignment format; BAM is the binary equivalent.
Tab-Separated Values: generic tabular data used for many genomics annotations and outputs.
WIG/Wiggle: dense continuous-valued tracks across the genome (e.g., coverage).
Variant Call Format: variants (SNPs, indels, SVs) with genotypes and annotations.
Binary VCF: compact, indexed binary representation of VCF.
General Feature Format: genomic features; GFF3 is the commonly used structured variant.
Gene Transfer Format: gene models/annotations; widely used with Ensembl/GENCODE.
Binary, indexed version of wiggle for efficient remote range queries in genome browsers.
Binary, indexed version of BED for efficient remote range queries in genome browsers.
JavaScript Object Notation: flexible metadata/annotations; structure is implementation-defined.
Extensible Markup Language: structured documents/metadata; schema-driven in some pipelines.
Hierarchical Data Format v5: container for large, structured arrays; used by some genomics tools.
